sources.citation: Chaudhary, Anil Dutt. 2020. Phonological study of the Sonaha language. Contemporary Research: An Interdisciplinary Academic Journal (CRAIAJ) 4(1): 15-33. doi:10.3126/craiaj.v4i1.32727 (= the ResearchGate item 346761434 named by the earlier scan; open on NepJOL)
sources.note: Nothing for Sonaha. Purely segmental: 6 vowels, 29 consonants (+4 residual breathy sonorants), syllable types V/CV/VC/CVC/CCV/CCVC, 7 vowel sequences. The single occurrence of the word 'stress' (p.17) is in the literature review describing Boehm (2003) on Dangaura Tharu, not Sonaha.

sources.citation: Bhasha Ayog [Language Commission, Nepal]. 2075 v.s. [2018]. Sonaha bhashako shabdasankalan [Word collection of the Sonaha language]. Test edition; research by Birendra Multiple Campus, Bharatpur (A. D. Chaudhary et al.). Kathmandu: Language Commission. 258 pp. (in Nepali)
sources.note: Nothing; sections 2.1-2.2 give consonant and vowel charts (Devanagari + IPA) used for transcribing the 3409-entry Sonaha-Nepali / Nepali-Sonaha wordlist; no suprasegmental statement.

sources.citation: Regmi, Dan Raj. 2015. Exploring relationships among the major Indo-Aryan languages of Tarai in Nepal. Nepalese Linguistics 30: 122-131.
sources.note: Nothing; lexicostatistic and phonetic-similarity clustering of Tarai Indo-Aryan varieties including Sonaha.

sources.citation: Thakur, Gopal & Indresh Thakur. 2014. A sociolinguistic survey of Sonaha and Khuna (as spoken in Bardiya, Kailali and Kanchanpur districts). Kathmandu: Linguistic Survey of Nepal (LinSuN), Central Department of Linguistics, Tribhuvan University. 178 pp.
sources.note: Nothing; sociolinguistic questionnaires, domains of use, vitality, lexical similarity, 210-word list in annex. No phonology chapter.

sources.citation: Linguistic Survey of Nepal (LinSuN). 2012. A sociolinguistic survey of Far-Western Development Region. Report submitted to the Ministry of Culture, Tourism and Civil Aviation. Kathmandu: CDL, TU. 292 pp. (Sonaha chapter by Indresh Thakur, pp.145 ff.)
sources.note: Nothing; the Sonaha chapter is sociolinguistic only (the one 'non-tonal' typology line in the volume refers to Raute).

sources.citation: Eberhard, David M., Gary F. Simons & Charles D. Fennig (eds.). Ethnologue: Languages of the World, entry Sonha [soi] (typology field).
sources.tag: likely states stress; not yet obtained
sources.note: Its typology line (source of Wikipedia's 'non-tonal') may also carry a stress remark derived from the LinSuN/SIL survey data; worth a one-line check by a subscriber.

sources.citation: Chaudhary, Anil Dutt, Bikram Chaudhary & P. Khanal. 2019. Sonaha bhashako bhashik itihas / Linguistic history of Sonaha. Report submitted to the Language Commission, Nepal (in Nepali).
sources.tag: likely states stress; not yet obtained
sources.note: Only other linguistic report on Sonaha by the sole phonology author; Language Commission 'language history' reports sometimes include a grammatical/phonological profile that could mention balaghat (stress).

sources.citation: Boehm, Edward Daniel. 1998. A phonological reconstruction of Proto-Tharu. M.A. thesis, University of Texas at Arlington; and Boehm, Kelly Kilgo / Boehm E. 2003 notes on Dangaura Tharu phonology (phoneme inventory, syllable types, stress) cited by Chaudhary 2020.

sources.note: Not Sonaha itself, but the closest described relative (Dangaura Tharu, ~80% intelligibility per Ethnologue) with an explicit stress section; would be the fallback proxy if the catalog accepts closely related Tharu varieties (different glottocode: dang1260).

sources.note: Abstract snippet only. The abstract reports a purely segmental profile (six vowels, twenty-nine consonants, six syllable types, seven vowel sequences), identical to Chaudhary 2020, within an ethnographic/historical overview; a suprasegmental remark (e.g. 'non-tonal') is possible but not seen. Likely largely derivative of the CRAIAJ article already listed here.
